utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, we are in open session now. Mr. Mundis.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. President, perhaps before the witness is brought back into the courtroom, in order to give effect to the Trial Chamber's rulings with respect to the daughter of the current witness, I'm not aware if that information has been communicated to VWS because we are in closed session --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Would you slow down Mr. Mundis, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: -- telephone to communicate that order.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. This morning, I took care that the Victims and Witness Units will be not too far away. The young lady -- is not too far away to get her into the public gallery. I don't know, Madam Registrar, who is supposed to give the information to the Witness and Victims Unit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So I do understand that the witness and victims -- Victim and Witness Section is informed about our decision, and we'll do whatever is necessary to give effect to our decision. Then, Mr. Mundis, I'll ask the usher to bring Mr. Pita into the courtroom so that you can continue to examine him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Can you hear me, Mr. Pita?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please be seated.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Although I think it might be unnecessary, but I'd just like to remind you that you're still bound by the solemn declaration you gave yesterday. Mr. Mundis will resume his examination. Please proceed, Mr. Mundis.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Examined by Mr. Mundis: [Continued]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Pita, can you tell the Chamber what your daughter Anisa was wearing when she was shot, that is, on December 13, 1992, what type of clothing she was wearing?

utterances.speaker: EKREM PITA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I already said she had sneakers, lace-up, trouser, a jacket, a cap on her head.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall what her friend Elma was wearing on that day?

utterances.speaker: EKREM PITA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, something similar except she didn't have the lace-up sneakers. She had something that looked more like slippers.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What were you wearing that day, Mr. Pita?

utterances.speaker: EKREM PITA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I was dressed as I'm usually dressed at home except that I had a jacket and trousers and kind of slippers, things that you wear around your home.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On the morning of 13 December, 1992, as you were walking to the source of the water, did you see any soldiers or other people wearing uniforms that morning?

utterances.speaker: EKREM PITA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no, no. I didn't. I didn't see anyone.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see any type of heavy military equipment or military weapons that morning as you were walking to the water source?

utterances.speaker: EKREM PITA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Where my house is, there is nothing. I never saw anything then or any time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I take it from that answer that as you returned from the water source, that is, as you are going back to your house, you also did not see any military equipment or any soldiers wearing uniforms that morning?

utterances.speaker: EKREM PITA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no, nothing. Nothing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you arrived back at your house that morning, you've testified that there were quite a few people in your house. Were any of those people wearing military uniforms?

utterances.speaker: EKREM PITA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Nobody.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were there any military weapons or heavy military equipment outside your house that morning?

utterances.speaker: EKREM PITA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, from what I know there, no, no. And I never noticed any.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: I would ask that the witness be shown the 360-degree panorama photo which has been marked P3279P.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Could the booth assist us -- no, it's not the booth. I make the same mistake as I did last time. The case manager is now putting the picture on the screen. Yes, please proceed, Mr. Mundis.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Pita, can you look at the screen in front of you and tell the Trial Chamber what is visible on the screen.

utterances.speaker: EKREM PITA [Resumed]
utterances.text: What you see is the entrance into the house, and the passage and the door to the living room.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The brown door on the centre right or the right centre of the photograph, is that the front door to your house?

utterances.speaker: EKREM PITA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: I'll ask that the photograph please be panned to the right. Pause there, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Pita, there appears to be a gate or a door in the centre of the photograph. Does that door or gate lead to the street that is in front of your house?

utterances.speaker: EKREM PITA [Resumed]
utterances.text: It does, yes. It does.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And in the lower centre of the photograph, there appears to be concrete. Is that what you refer to as the terrace or the balcony of your house?

utterances.speaker: EKREM PITA [Resumed]
utterances.text: From the gate towards the house, about 2 metres is this entrance. And then after 2 metres or so of this concrete slab, there's some stairs, and then comes the terrace.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Could you please pan the photograph further to the right. Please pause there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is the area shown on the lower right hand portion of this photograph now visible, the area that you refer to as the terrace?

utterances.speaker: EKREM PITA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. That is the terrace.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: I'd ask that the photograph, please, be panned upwards. And if we could then zoom in, please. That's fine. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Pita, off in the distance, beyond the tree branch that's in the immediate -- the front of the picture, can you tell us what's visible in the background at the upper centre portion of the picture that's in front of you, please.

utterances.speaker: EKREM PITA [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I can see, it is those two facilities from which Anisa was targeted presumably. Those up there. It's so-called Baba Stijena, Baba rock.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Approximately how far from your terrace is the Baba rock located?

utterances.speaker: EKREM PITA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said it yesterday. I said that I was not an expert so I don't really know. It can be 350, 550 as the crow flies.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Which armed force or forces controlled the Baba stone or Baba rocks?

utterances.speaker: EKREM PITA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said it yesterday, it was the army of Republika Srpska and the former Yugoslav army.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you. If the photograph can be zoomed back outwards. And please continue panning to the right. That's fine. Thank you very much. I'd ask that the witness now be shown the photograph marked P3267, please. I'd ask that the usher please place that photograph on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Pita, I'd ask you to take a look at the photograph which is visible to your right. Perhaps on the screen in front of you. Can you tell us -- can you tell us where this photograph was taken?

utterances.speaker: EKREM PITA [Resumed]
utterances.text: The photograph was taken approximately from the entrance from the steps to the -- from the gate to the steps to the terrace approximately from there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That would be approximately the area inside the gates on the lower concrete area that you previously identified in the last electronic photograph? Is that correct, Mr. Pita?

utterances.speaker: EKREM PITA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And on a previous occasion, in 2001, were you shown this photograph by an investigator from the Tribunal?

utterances.speaker: EKREM PITA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you, in fact, make some markings with a black marker on this photograph?

utterances.speaker: EKREM PITA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I draw this line around, this shape. And I put -- there's a rose here, and then I put an arrow to where the firing came from. That's what I believe. There's no other location where it could have come from, not even theoretically.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This small tree that's in the -- enclosed within the line that you drew, why did you circle that tree?

utterances.speaker: EKREM PITA [Resumed]
utterances.text: We circled it because there were no -- there were no other trees, neither higher than lower. It wasn't there. My brothers planted it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That tree was planted after the war. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: EKREM PITA [Resumed]
utterances.text: After we left the country, so it wasn't there before.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when you say "left the country," that was to seek medical treatment for your second daughter. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: EKREM PITA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: I'd ask that the witness now be shown the video which has been marked P3280P, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If the booth could assist us. Yes, I see it's already on the screen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: "INVESTIGATOR ON TAPE: Could you please show me by pointing where, to the best of your recollection, you heard gunfire shortly before your daughter Anisa was shot. "Thank you. Could you now please show me where, to the best of your recollection, the bullet hole was before the wall was repaired. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. "I can see traces of repair work on the wall at this location, and I am going to place a small red marks with a red tip felt pen."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Pita, did you recognise yourself in that videotape?

utterances.speaker: EKREM PITA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And to the best of your recollection, did you comply with the directions of the investigator truthfully and honestly?

utterances.speaker: EKREM PITA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, I think so.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yesterday you testified that while you and your wife and your daughter were at the hospital, your brother found the bullet that struck your daughter. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: EKREM PITA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the spot in the lower part of the door frame that you indicated to the investigator was the spot where the bullet struck the wall after striking your daughter. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: EKREM PITA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You also told us yesterday that after your daughter was released from the hospital, that you had to take her back for periodic medical treatment. Do you remember saying that?

utterances.speaker: EKREM PITA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I remember. That's exactly how it was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Approximately -- for approximately how long -- withdraw that question. How long after your daughter was discharged from the hospital did this periodic medical treatment continue?

utterances.speaker: EKREM PITA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Approximately we took her for three weeks, every three or four days, as the doctors told us, for a checkup and also for a change of bandages.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you describe for the Trial Chamber how you took your daughter to the hospital for those periodic checkups?

utterances.speaker: EKREM PITA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can. My wife and I took her, but we didn't take her. We had to carry her from my house to the hospital. There is roughly 3 or 4 kilometres, and we had to carry her. And it was very dangerous. We had to take very dangerous streets under fire. As I said yesterday, and I'm repeating it, these moments were far worse for me because when she was wounded, I saw that she was all right, that she was going to be all right. But then I thought what is going to happen if something happens to us on the way to the hospital or the way back from the hospital. And then of course she wouldn't go to the hospital. Then she would say well I will go to the hospital if you buy me a chocolate. I had to convince her. One chocolate to the way there and one for the way back. It was very difficult.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Pita. The Prosecution has no further questions at this time, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Mundis. Ms. Pilipovic, Defence is ready to cross-examine the witness?

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Pita, questions will now be put to you by counsel for the Defence. Please proceed, Ms. Pilipovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. Cross-examined by Ms. Pilipovic:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Pita, good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: EKREM PITA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yesterday during the examination-in-chief by my learned colleague, you said that until the beginning of the conflict in Sarajevo, you worked in Union Invest as an electrician. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: EKREM PITA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell us until when did you work in Union Invest as an electrician, until what day did you go to work?

utterances.speaker: EKREM PITA [Resumed]
utterances.text: To tell you exactly, after November 1991, I did not go to work. I was then on a waiting list. There was no work in the company.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So what you're saying, that from November 1991, you did not go to work, to the building of Union Invest, that's where your working place was?

utterances.speaker: EKREM PITA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not work there in the building of Union Invest. I was working in different facilities, in different buildings.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell us from November 1991, since you were on a waiting schedule, did you do any other kind of work? Did you work somewhere else as an electrician?

utterances.speaker: EKREM PITA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I worked privately in the town somewhere. In different places.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say that you worked privately and in the city, until when did you work privately in the city?

utterances.speaker: EKREM PITA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I worked until the 4th of April, and I even worked on that day.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say that you worked until the 4th of April, 1992, are you telling us that after that, you did not work any more?

utterances.speaker: EKREM PITA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not work after that. It was not possible to walk around. I came back home, and I did not move from -- did not go out of my neighbourhood.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The neighbourhood where you lived in, does it have a specific name? What part of town is it?

utterances.speaker: EKREM PITA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said it yesterday.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, you said it was Stari Grad, old town.

utterances.speaker: EKREM PITA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said it was Stari Grad, old town Sirokaca.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the Defence would like to show the witness that section of the map so that the witness could mark for us on the map this old town Sirokaca and approximately where his house was, if we can then have a picture of this neighbourhood as the witness says. We have got copies of the map of town, and then using the map, we would like to ask some more questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please proceed, Ms. Pilipovic, and I'll ask the usher to assist you in distributing the copies.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The number for the map will be D49.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Pita, you have before you a portion of the map of the city. The Defence copied the part of town which encompasses your area of town, Sirokaca. Could you perhaps circle on this map that you can see next to you using the black pen the Sirokaca.

utterances.speaker: EKREM PITA [Resumed]
utterances.text: To tell you the truth, I cannot see it there. I mean...

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Pita, perhaps you could use a pen so that we can see it on our screens, so that we can all see it on our screens.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Pita, could you please leave it on the screen to the right of you because that's how we get the picture on our screen.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Pita, you circled just the name Sirokaca. You marked the area Sirokaca. Could you perhaps put number 1 on that circle so that we know that that is Sirokaca.

utterances.speaker: EKREM PITA [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Then, in relation to this circle, could you perhaps mark the place within or outside of the circle where your house was -- where your house is.

utterances.speaker: EKREM PITA [Resumed]
utterances.text: The street is not on there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was the name of the street, or what is the name of the street if the name didn't change?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness repeat the name of the street.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Pita, could you please repeat your answer as to what street your house was located.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Zagrici Street.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, if we look at the circle that you marked as number 1, a little bit to the left you will see that there is a street called Zagrici there. Is that your street where you lived? On the left-hand side, if you can see from this fork, from these forking streets in relation to the circle.

utterances.speaker: EKREM PITA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't see it, but I lived on that street and I still live on that street.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You can see above the circle on the left-hand side there is a street called Zagrici. The circle doesn't encompass it all. You probably didn't see it very well.

utterances.speaker: EKREM PITA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, well, I don't have very good eyesight. I cannot see it very well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If I tell you that it says Zagrici, would you then agree?

utterances.speaker: EKREM PITA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, if it says, that then it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well you cannot see the Z because you marked it with a black pen.

utterances.speaker: EKREM PITA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is the street. That's the street.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Pita. Considering that you told us that you live in this area, in this circle that you marked, could you tell us whether the source of this water that you went to fetch, is it within the circle as well?

utterances.speaker: EKREM PITA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it's not. The source is not. The source is to the left, on my left.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you perhaps mark it on the map for us, this location where you went with Anisa to fetch the water.

utterances.speaker: EKREM PITA [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Perhaps it will be easier to orientate yourself.

utterances.speaker: EKREM PITA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot tell you for sure.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We don't need you to be absolutely certain.

utterances.speaker: EKREM PITA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that it is to the left side. As well, looking at the picture, it's to the left.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it in relation --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Pilipovic, may I ask you, you know the technique better than the witness who is just looking at the screen and sees the picture at this moment to make a pause between the answer and your next question. Mr. Pita, you and Ms. Pilipovic are using the same language, and if you respond immediately once you heard the question, the interpreters will not be able to translate quick enough what you said. And since we are all very much interested to hear what your answer to the questions is, could you also make a brief pause before you answer the questions.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Pita, could you tell us, give us an estimate, how far away from your house this source is, is it a metre or kilometre?

utterances.speaker: EKREM PITA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said it was about 150 metres from my house. It was not a real source. It was just a man who was using surface water with a pipe. It's not really a source.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. When you told us that from April, you did not go into the city, did I understand you correctly?

utterances.speaker: EKREM PITA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did go when I really had to.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell us in this part of the city where you lived, were there any incidents? Did you notice any clashes?

utterances.speaker: EKREM PITA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no, clashes. I did not notice. I never saw anything, and I don't know anything about it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you give us an answer, looking at the house on the street where you lived, do you know anything -- do you know anything about a location that you knew that the units of the BH army or the VRS army were based?

utterances.speaker: EKREM PITA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I couldn't know that. I told you the BH army, I don't know where they were based. I was not -- I was not a member of the army. I had family and personal problems from the start. So I wouldn't know. From that house, you could see that there are those marks from shelling.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You told us now that you were not engaged in the BH army because you had family problems. Could you tell us on what kind of information are you -- on the basis of what information are you telling us that if we're looking -- if we're looking at the Baba rock, and your house, how can you tell that the Baba rock was under that control, under the control of the Serb army?

utterances.speaker: EKREM PITA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, because from my house you can see it. You can see it from the street. And it is -- it was obvious that this was used by the VRS army. You can see that the street below was used, and you can see it even now that there was a hole and there were two trenches. So it's a very simple issue.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On the map which is before you, could you mark in relation to the street where you lived? A part of your neighbourhood or above your neighbourhood where the Baba rock is?

utterances.speaker: EKREM PITA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot see it on this particular image.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But if you look at the map, on the right-hand side, on your right side, on the map, perhaps you can see it a bit better.

utterances.speaker: EKREM PITA [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is possible to see, but I can't really.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Pita, could you please look at the map as it is on the machine. Perhaps, Mr. Usher, could you assist, because that map is bigger than what you see on the screen. So the question is whether you can identify this particular rock on the map.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, I have a very bad eyesight, and I really can't find my bearings on this map.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Pilipovic, if the witness is not able to -- you might have seen it. I even use my glasses now and then. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you're telling us that this rock is called Baba, could you tell us, is this an area of the town, or is it some kind of high ground, some elevation where a rock is?

utterances.speaker: EKREM PITA [Resumed]
utterances.text: The rock is called Baba. That's what we called it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you perhaps give us a description. When we say a "rock" is it some kind of a hill? When we say rock, we mean a rock. Is this some kind of an elevation in relation to your house?

utterances.speaker: EKREM PITA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it's an elevation. It's a rock above the house.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You told us that in relation to your house as the crow flies, about 250, 300 metres, you did not measure it?

utterances.speaker: EKREM PITA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not measure it, and I don't know. I'm not an expert.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you go to that rock, for instance, in 1992, 1993, or 1995, or 1998 when you returned?

utterances.speaker: EKREM PITA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have never been to the rock, and I never intend to go to the rock.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you go before the incident happened?

utterances.speaker: EKREM PITA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I never went. Perhaps before the war, maybe for picnics I went, long before the war.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How long -- how long would it take you to get to the rock? How many kilometres even if you walked or if you took any kind of transport?

utterances.speaker: EKREM PITA [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was perhaps a kilometre and a half, something like that. 1.000, 1.200 metres. But really, I never measured it so I don't know. There are experts I'm sure who can work it out.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell us, since you told us already that you left Sarajevo for family reasons, and you returned in 1998, can you tell me -- can you tell us when you left Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: EKREM PITA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I left Sarajevo on 24th of March, 1994.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So from December 1992, and the moment when the incident happened and your daughter was wounded, until the moment you left Sarajevo, you said that you often went for checkups with your daughter. Can you tell us in that period on the way to the hospital or to the medical centre, did you see soldiers?

utterances.speaker: EKREM PITA [Resumed]
utterances.text: To tell you the truth, I never saw anyone, not in that part of the road, never. I was never interested in that. I've got to explain you something. In the beginning of the war, my father died. My wife had a mastectomy. I really had a lot of problems to do with my family. I'm not interested in it even really today. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell us, on that day when the incident happened and when you entered the house, in talking to your daughter and to your wife, did you find out in which position was your daughter standing at the moment when she was wounded?

utterances.speaker: EKREM PITA [Resumed]
utterances.text: To tell you the truth, you can imagine what it was like when I entered the house. At that time, I didn't ask any questions. I did not really feel very well, but I had to be the first one to react because nobody would react. So whatever happened I would -- I took her, returned. We did talk about it. I asked her -- I asked my wife, and she said Anisa was turned. She was facing the door, and she was bending over to do her -- to take her sneakers off because the wife had told her to take the sneakers off because she had just cleaned the -- cleaned the house so that she wouldn't make it dirty. And as she was undoing the sneakers, this is what happened, and this is when my little girl started to cry. Sorry. And then my wife reacted, asked her what happened, and then what happened is that my little girl screamed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Considering that you showed us on the 360-degree photograph, you showed us the entrance door, the spot where you presume the bullet struck, do you allow for the possibility that the bullet ricochetted on the door?

utterances.speaker: EKREM PITA [Resumed]
utterances.text: This was not the door, this was the corner of the wall.

utterances.speaker: EKREM PITA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't know. If it had, then it would have gone in a different direction. I'm telling you, Anisa was wounded in the upper leg, in her thigh. So probably what happened was the bullet went from the inner thigh, at the inner thigh and then exited the other side of the thigh. And then struck the wall. That's probably what happened.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that your brother found the bullet?

utterances.speaker: EKREM PITA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did your brother tell you where he found it?

utterances.speaker: EKREM PITA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he did. He said he found it in one of the slippers that were there, that were just there on the floor, on the ground or somewhere under the slippers. That's what he said. I didn't ask many questions, to be honest. He just told me that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you're telling us that you never saw the bullet?

utterances.speaker: EKREM PITA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did see the bullet. He told me how he found, it and then when I saw the bullet, I did not want to keep it or look at it or have anything to do with it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Today we were able to see on the 360-degrees photograph the terrace in front of your house. Could you tell us, as you go out on to your terrace, apart from seeing the hill that you say is Baba, that you can see Baba rock, what other parts of town in relation to that side or the hills, what other parts of town or hills? What do you see when you come out on to the terrace? Because we could see that there was another house on the other side. What else do you see?

utterances.speaker: EKREM PITA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Nothing much. When you come out of the terrace, I can see another house, of course now today there are more houses, but I'm talking about then. There was one house, and then there was a cemetery up there, higher up. There was -- at the time, Sarajevo, there was not enough wood, firewood, so they would be cutting wood. Of course, none of this would have happened had there been trees there. But of course they had been cut down so you could see everything.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Pita, you are talking quite quickly, which I understand. But we would like to hear whatever you say to us, and it first has to be translated. So if it would be possible, would you please slow down a bit, and then Ms. Pilipovic waits before she puts a new question to you. If you see the text on the screen, perhaps you could wait to answer the question up to the moment where it stops moving. Yes. I have a full understanding, but we would really like to hear what you tell us. Please proceed, Ms. Pilipovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, you told us that you could see Hambina Carina and the cemetery. Can you tell us in relation to the circle where you put number 1, can you also circle the -- this area where you say that one can see the cemetery and Hambina Carina?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Usher, could you please --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can't see.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Pita, perhaps if you -- I'm sorry. Mr. Pita, perhaps you first look at the screen where it is larger. Mr. Usher, could you please then move the map a bit to the right. A bit more to the right so that we can see at least the 1. Put the 1 in the centre of the -- yes. Perhaps it could be zoomed in now a bit. Please stop. Can you see it now on the screen, Mr. Pita?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes, I see it. Yes, I see it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Can you try to also find it on the map on the right-hand side of you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'll try.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And then circle the area where you said you could see the cemetery and Hambina Carina.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can't read this.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, with your leave, for the record, can the witness tell us in relation to this circle -- he need not circle it -- does he see that under -- that below this circle is the Hambina Carina part of the road.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: EKREM PITA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And above the line where it says "Hambina Carina," then there was a cemetery. Is that what you are talking about?

utterances.speaker: EKREM PITA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you then tell us in relation to the cemetery that you see, is the hill that you can see beyond the street Cicin Han or the street Hambina Carina?

utterances.speaker: EKREM PITA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Cicin Han I can see. That street, as far as I know, it goes right through the middle of the cemetery. It goes through the cemetery.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And where, if it can be precise, in relation to Cicin Han, in relation to the Hambina Carina cemetery, where is this Baba rock? Where is this elevation, where you say is this in relation to Cicin Han Street or Hambina Carina?

utterances.speaker: EKREM PITA [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is over Hambina Carina from my house and over Hambina Carina and that would be the direction.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We see here Braykovac, Cicin Han. Would you allow that it is in that part of, that is below Hambina Carina? Is that elevation Baba rock there?

utterances.speaker: EKREM PITA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Baba rock is to the right of Braykovac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it in relation to this part where it says Lipe?

utterances.speaker: EKREM PITA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it is not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Not where it says Lipe?

utterances.speaker: EKREM PITA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let me tell you. I don't really know these streets, and I can't find my way particularly around them. I told you, I was not hit. But from that place I told you there is my house, one house above me, and then you can see the cemetery, and beyond the cemetery is this rock, Baba. That's what I'm telling you. This way, I can't do it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you have any knowledge, if in 1992, 1993 who lived in those houses that you say you could see from your terrace?

utterances.speaker: EKREM PITA [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was one man less than 50 metres away, there was a neighbour of mine who lived in that house and who still lives there for that matter.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On the basis of your statement, we learned that the incident happened in December, or to be precise, and so that I don't ask you again, it was the 13th of December, 1992. Can you tell us whether that day or that night, whether you could hear if there was any gunfire in relation to that part of the city in which you lived?

utterances.speaker: EKREM PITA [Resumed]
utterances.text: That night was quiet. There was no gunfire, nothing. There would be a shot here and there. And in the morning, I wouldn't have gone with the child to fetch that water had there been any gunfire, but it was all quiet. There was nothing, nothing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You told us that it was foggy in the morning.

utterances.speaker: EKREM PITA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I said, yes, it was hazy. It was overcast. That is what I said.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you said that you went around 10 or half past 10.00. You were not precise, that you left the house. Can you tell us what the weather was like then?

utterances.speaker: EKREM PITA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I've already said. It was overcast, and there were those patches of fog, that is, it was slightly hazy. I'm telling you again I wouldn't have taken my child along if I thought we wouldn't get through. 40 minutes, half an hour, I don't know how long we were there, I could see that everything was clear. And then when the shot, it was the house, I told the Elma, the older one, just look out and at that moment the gunfire started.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Pita, may I remind you to slow down a bit. Because they first have to listen to you, and then they have to translate it, only then can we hear it. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could you remove this slide from the screen, because then I could have some control. As it is now, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Do you still need the map, Ms. Pilipovic, or? No, then please, Mr. Usher, would you change the screen again. Do you see the text now again?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, you said that you -- that you had problems in your family, and that you were not interested in matters military, to simplify it. What about your brothers, those who lived nearby, your brother from your proper family. Was any of them a member of the BH army, and did he tell you if there was any fighting in that part of the city?

utterances.speaker: EKREM PITA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let me tell you, I did not communicate, and we didn't talk about it. I do not know that. I didn't talk to them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In relation to the time when the incident happened on the 13th of December, 1992, can you tell us how many days before that did you hear whether there was any gunfire and at what time?

utterances.speaker: EKREM PITA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't really remember. All I know is that sometime in June, five or six shells fell around my house. That is the gate, the garage, the house, and one could hear quite often the rifle. I mean, there was often fire.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say there was fire often, how often is that in relation to a month or a week?

utterances.speaker: EKREM PITA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. Well, there would be every day, there would be a bullet or two or several times. We spent most of the time in the cellar so that we didn't...

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us how often -- and when I say "often," I mean in relation to a week -- how often did you go to that part to fetch water, to that part in relation to your house to that part of the city or to the neighbourhood? How often did you go?

utterances.speaker: EKREM PITA [Resumed]
utterances.text: We went when the need arose.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say you went when the need arose, can you be more specific and tell us what does this need mean? Per week or a day?

utterances.speaker: EKREM PITA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, a day, well, one -- well, when my wife said we needed some water, then we would go there. I can't say whether it was a week or a day. You know how things happen.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that there was fire often. Can you tell us from which directions and from which parts of the city did you hear this gunfire?

utterances.speaker: EKREM PITA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot tell you about other parts of the city. I can talk about my area only. It was above our houses up there, and I told you from those positions. I've told you that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you have any knowledge that from these positions from which you say the gunfire came, do you know if that fire was returned towards those positions?

utterances.speaker: EKREM PITA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, just a second. Let me consult my co-counsel to see if we have any further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please do so, Ms. Pilipovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the Defence has no further questions. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Ms. Pilipovic. Mr. Mundis, any need to re-examine the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: No, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Pita, since the Bench has no further questions for you, this ends your examination as a witness in this courtroom. Please be aware that this Court understands quite well what it is for you to come the long way from Sarajevo to The Hague, and I hope that you'll be convinced that this Court finds it very important that all the questions put by the parties are answered by those who were present in the area and at the relevant time. So therefore, we thank you very much in assisting the parties and the Court which finally should result in decisions we'll have to take. And I wish you a safe trip home again.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Usher, would you then please lead the witness out of the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Mundis, I don't know whether you're going to ask for a break in order to prepare the courtroom for the next witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: I was going to ask for a break so that the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Especially the voice distortion takes some time to be prepared. After we have done with the document, I think we have four documents, Madam Registrar, tendered in evidence. Would you please...

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The 360-degree Quicktime movie will be P327P. And the video, P3280P. The photograph, P3267; and the map marked by the witness, D49.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: They are then admitted into evidence. We're now just a couple of minutes after half past 3.00. I suggest that we have a break now so that the courtroom can be prepared for the next witness. We'll resume at 4.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: For the benefit of the microphone, there is no transcript.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I see there is transcript now.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, not only is there no transcript of what Mr. Piletta-Zanin said, but there is no translation as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NIETO-NAVIA
utterances.text: I think that the problem is the French is on channel 4.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes, I'm hearing French on channel 4.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I have changed, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now I have the English on channel 4 again.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And channel 5, we have now. [French spoken]. This also has caused the words spoken by Mr. Piletta-Zanin not to be translated. So would you please repeat what you said, Mr. Piletta-Zanin. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. You have drawn the attention, perhaps I can resume it. You asked attention for the back pain suffered by General Galic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] [French spoken] Is there any problem with the translation, Mr. Ierace, or you want me to do it in English? If you have any problem with French, it would be my privilege of doing so, so just tell me what you want.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, my French is improving but it's not yet anywhere near the high standard of my learned colleague.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And channel 4, do you have English or French now?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Again, I had French when my friend was speaking. It was English just before then, with the "1, 2, 3."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, would you please speak French now, Mr. Piletta-Zanin, so that we can see whether there's any translation. [French spoken].

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] [French spoken].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [French spoken].

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: We have only French on channel 4.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And we have English on? [Interpretation] When I speak French, I only hear my French on channel 5. When I speak French and when I listen to channel 4, I hear English, the English interpretation. [In English] So as far as I can see, we have now English on channel 4, and French on channel 5. Please proceed, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] [No interpretation].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I once again hear French on channel 4. Well, as far as I'm concerned, I'm perfectly happy, but I do not know what I can do. [In English] Yes, now I hear English again on channel 4. So please proceed, Mr. Piletta-Zanin, in French, and we'll just listen whether we have the translation on channel 4.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Does it work now? I was saying, so that everybody can understand, that during the break, we met with the General Galic, and he says that the pain is practically unbearable. Therefore, it is absolutely necessary to organise a visit to a doctor as quickly as possible. Tomorrow, if possible, because if the medical authorities think it useful, perhaps General Galic could be helped by some therapeutical means which will be better and which will enable him to attend the hearing regularly, but we need the assistance of the Chamber.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. We will see that we get in touch with those responsible for the medical treatment. Perhaps if one of you could -- of the Defence team could try to get in touch with OLAD right away. That's the best way to promote the medical treatment, of course, if possible. You know that a lot of Dutch citizens have to wait for a very long time until they can see a doctor. So whatever will be possible will be best promoted by addressing the OLAD immediately. May I just ask an additional question: For this afternoon, General Galic could stay in the courtroom? It's not that urgent, without denying the urgency and the severity?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you for your question, Mr. President. I don't want to give an answer for Mr. Galic but I believe he is being very stoical about this and I think he can keep up this afternoon unless there's a change, in which case he will tell us. He may well have to leave. But perhaps somebody else would leave and call competent people who could perhaps help, if you will allow us.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Someone else; who would you have in mind at this moment?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] [Previous translation continues]...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but could you address the OLAD people right away? Perhaps that takes five minutes or...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar tells me that she could try to get in touch with one of the OLAD people so that you can have a very short conference right away so that you can --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] From the inside of the Chamber, of the courtroom?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, she can call from the inside of the courtroom, and that perhaps this will cause your absence for five minutes so that you can explain.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: General Galic, apart from the measures we are trying to take now, I'd just like to hear from you as well, whether you agree with Mr. Piletta-Zanin that although you do not feel well, that you are still able to continue this afternoon?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have already said that I can stay here unless, of course, I feel very bad, and then I will say so. But you need to understand one thing, that this pain moves from my spine down my legs, and then back to my head, so that is my problem. I did undergo treatment here. You know that at the time of my arrest, I was severely injured, and for six months I could not move my right foot. I have three injuries along my spine, the scanning established that. It was established in the detention unit and it was established that I have a herniated disk which could be treated if I gave-- did not do physical work. But how can I do that if I cannot walk. I mean, it hurts. And then a surgical intervention was suggested to me, and you remember this whole discussion. I said that I would try to suffer this pain as long as I can because it is in my interest to finish the trial as quickly and as soon as possible. That is my objective. I will do my best. But if it becomes too hard for me, then I will ask for the floor without any fear, without any ill effect. I believe that I can follow the proceedings, and that I'll be able to do so tomorrow. But it is quite possible of course. I do not know why I am not knowledgeable about things. Perhaps tomorrow morning I should be given an injection or something in addition to the medicines that are administered every day. Perhaps an injection would allay the pain somewhat for tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Whenever you feel that you're -- that you cannot follow the proceedings any more, as you told us already, you'd be on your feet and tell us immediately. That's what I invite you to do if necessary. And meanwhile, I think your counsel together with the OLAD see that as soon as possible an appointment with a specialist will be made when necessary.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I do hear that it might be possible to be examined by a doctor tomorrow in the afternoon presumably. I don't know whether this will already be a specialist or that you will first be seen by the general practitioner, but you'll then certainly know how to proceed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The OLAD will be in touch with the detention unit and see whether this can be arranged even for tomorrow. If the appointment could be made in the afternoon, could we expect you to be in the courtroom in the morning or...

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, absolutely.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you very much. We will then pay proper attention to it. And I'm glad that I raised the issue today. General Galic, we discussed the matter in open court, and since I know that you are not very favourable of talking with everyone about these kind of problems, there has been no one here. Would it be necessary to do the whole thing of redacting or would you just accept the way we discussed it as it is now. Redacting, I mean to change the transcript or that we just accept as it is now the transcript. We didn't go in any detail, I think.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, it can stay. There's -- I don't want to be someone who is complicating the matters.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I'm much obliged to this attitude. Thank you. Then, before we continue, I have one other issue I'd like to discuss with the parties at this time. During the break, I saw a decision of the Registry, a decision appointing a presiding officer to witness the declaration of a witness in The Hague today. The Rule 92 bis is usually applied when there's some difficulty in having the witnesses in this courtroom. I wondered, since this witness seems to be in The Hague, what actually was the specific reason not to hear this witness in this courtroom, being the witness in The Hague, and I also would like to know whether we could find some kind of a procedure that if there's any need of cross-examining a witness, that we could at least use his or her presence at this moment in The Hague. Because if the witness -- I don't know who the witness is. I don't know whether the witness lives in the Netherlands or in the former Yugoslavia or wherever. But I know for sure that if there would be a request later on to cross-examine the witness for specific reasons, then it would not be easy perhaps to get the witness again in the Netherlands if the witness is not residing in the Netherlands at this very moment. So if you could please clarify this, Mr. Ierace. And Mr. Piletta-Zanin, you would like to --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, this is just to say we do not know who this witness is. We don't have any information, so we will be listening with great interest. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ierace. I don't know whether it's a protected witness. I've got no idea. So would you please be very careful since we are dealing with it at this moment in open Court.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I will make some inquiries as to the identity of the particular witness, but in the meantime I will say this: During the pre-trial stage, the Prosecution was encouraged by the Pre-Trial Chamber to have as many witnesses as possible dealt with by way of the Rule 92 bis procedure. In other words, in the interests of saving Court time. I have not previously understood that it was a prerequisite to the use of Rule 92 bis that there be an impediment to the witness giving evidence in the Trial Chamber. I had understood that a primary purpose was to save time in the Trial Chamber, and that, I confess, has been my guiding principle in selecting 92 bis witnesses. I will give you more information when I clarify the identity of the particular witness. Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I do not think that you misunderstood what was said during the pre-trial proceedings, only as far as I'm aware of, very often the procedure of 92 bis is used for witnesses that are not living near to the seat of the Tribunal. And if there's any need to cross-examine the witness on the basis of the statement given by the witness, then of course it would be perhaps not very efficient to let the witness return to a place far away from the seat of the Court, and perhaps then we would even have to call the witness again if we would allow the cross-examination of the witness upon the request of the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, might I say something about that: My preference would have been that we decide which witnesses can give their evidence by way of 92 bis before the 92 bis procedure is taken. I made some inquiries, and the result of those inquiries was that it was unfortunately necessary to go to this trouble to obtain the statement in 92 bis form before we could invite you, the Trial Chamber, to rule on that. I agree it would have been far more sensible if we simply could have handed up a copy of the statement and had a ruling on the basis of the statement because, ultimately, if any of the 92 bis witnesses are rejected by the Trial Chamber, there has been a considerable waste of time by both the OTP and the Registry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Of course, I have concentrated on the issue of 92 bis before as well, and I also found that it's the order, we'll find, in the Rules and also in the Practice Directions is that it should be done as it is done at this very moment. This leaves apart the possibility of perhaps introducing this statement of this very witness a bit earlier so that, if the witness is still in The Hague, that there might be -- that we might give a judgment now on whether, if there's any need to cross-examine the witness, that we can decide on the issue now before the witness has returned to the place where the witness is residing. Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. I think that the Defence -- it would have been helpful for the Defence if we could have the name of the witness because that would have -- that would be of assistance, particularly because, if I am to understand, that the Chamber does appreciate precision. Now, there is a problem, Mr. President, more important than the identity of the witness that we at the moment have no idea of, which is the principle, Mr. President. And I would like to just take a few moments to say more about this. On several occasions, we heard witnesses, and these witnesses, when they were cross-examined by the Defence, they said things that were unexpected but very useful for the Defence. And we could think of a witness that, in front of his window, there was an HQ on the front line, in front of his window. Or perhaps we could think of another witness who -- who said that he was accompanied by a soldier when he was injured, and we are talking about the young man who testified a few days ago who was 25 years old, or perhaps we could think of other witnesses who would then tell us about important things after being questioned, and that there were brigades or troops stationed near their place of residence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think what you're doing now is already entering into a debate on whether 92 bis witnesses -- and as we all know that you have filed your view on 92 bis witnesses at the Registry. Once the Prosecution has given notice to you that they intended to use statements of witnesses on the basis of 92 bis. We'll deal with that in a later stage, and I would rather not have this debate at this very moment. The only exception I'd like to make is that perhaps on the witness which, apparently, is in The Hague at this very moment, that if there's any need to cross-examine that witness, that perhaps we use -- we should use the presence of the witness in The Hague.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I think that the occasion is here. I think we should seize this opportunity, and the witness could certainly come and testify, as I said a moment ago.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, the witness will be presented as a 92 bis statement. Once the Chamber has read the statement before giving its decision whether it accepts this evidence as a statement rather than a viva voce testimony of the witness, we'll decide on whether we'll accept the evidence, then the Defence can make an application showing good cause why the witness still should be cross-examined by the Defence, and we'll then take a decision on that. But I'll just try to speed up this for a witness which turns out to be in The Hague at this very moment. I would then like to proceed and to call the -- have the next witness of the Prosecution called, Mr. Ierace. Perhaps you could solve things out during the next break, and then that we proceed now.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. The next witness is Witness E. Before the witness is called, I should inform the Trial Chamber that the video in respect of this incident has not redacted -- has not been redacted at this stage, and therefore I seek that the showing of the video be done in closed session. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then Madam Registrar, everything is functioning as it should function as far as the face and the voice alteration is concerned? Then I see that the usher left the courtroom ready to bring in witness E.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: While the witness is coming in, perhaps at this stage I could alert the Trial Chamber to a problem that I have become aware of. I don't yet have a solution to the problem. The scheduled incidents to Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. the indictment are not in redacted form and never have been. That is because the relevant witnesses have indicated their desire for protective measures at a later point. The end result of that is that when I identify the particular incident, potential allows for the identification of the witness. Even the reference to the date would allow that. It's a difficult issue. For that reason, from here on in, I propose to have the witness give evidence of the date in written form. That will at least assist. And once you, Mr. President, and Your Honours, and the Defence have seen that date, it will be a relatively simple matter to identify which of the incidents on the schedule the evidence relates to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Perhaps we could proceed in a similar way as with the name and the date of birth. So if you would prepare -- well, perhaps you could do it right away. A similar sheet provided with a number, and then show it to the witness, give a copy to the Court, give a copy to the Defence, and then we'll ask her to read the date and indicate to her that whenever we'll talk about the incident, that we are referring to an incident of that date. Another way would be that we ask her not to answer any question as far as the date of the incident is concerned, but to ask her to write it down on paper and then admit that document into evidence. Perhaps that would be a more correct way of doing it. Just one second.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Defence is ready?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, ready to answer, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In relation to the proceedings, we have no objections to the witness writing every time. Of course, no problem whatsoever.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I would not have the witness to write everything down. So we'll then proceed. But may I remind the parties that they put off their microphones once they have put the questions to the witness since the voice distortion might not function well if you leave your microphones open. Please, then, Mr. Usher, bring in the courtroom in the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Can you hear me in a language you understand?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I will call you Miss E since protective measures are taken in respect of you. So I'll not use your name. I'll you "Miss E" during your presence in this courtroom. First of all, welcome in this courtroom. Before you give testimony in this Court, the Rules of Procedure and Evidence require you to make a solemn declaration that you'll speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth. And the text of this solemn declaration will be handed out to you now by the usher, and I invite you to make that declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Miss E. Please be seated. You have been called as a witness by the Prosecution, so the order of your examination is that you'll first be examined by counsel for the Prosecution. You'll then be examined by counsel for the Defence, and if there are any additional questions to be put by the Bench we'll do so as well. Mr. Ierace, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Examined by Mr. Ierace:

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I ask that the witness be given Exhibit P3564.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are the details on the sheet of paper in front of you correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I seek to tender that exhibit as a confidential exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P3654 is admitted into evidence under seal.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: For the benefit of the transcript, that contains the witness's name and date of birth.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where were you living --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I would like to intervene on behalf of the French booth, complaining that they cannot hear Mr. Ierace. I don't know whether that's channel 5, 4, or 3, but Mr. Ierace cannot be heard by the booth.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I will speak up.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where were you living in 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E
utterances.text: In Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you continue to live in Sarajevo throughout the armed conflict?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: We cannot hear the witness at all. We are sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Usher, could you please assist the witness. I see that the microphones are not in her direction. The interpreters' booth complains that they cannot hear the witness. I'm informed that channel 7 could assist the interpreters' booth. Could you please say a few words, Miss E, in order to test all the technical stuff which is found in this courtroom. Could you just say a few words, like "Dubra Dom." Does this give a satisfactory result in the --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Not really. There is still very faint sound from the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you speak a bit louder, Miss E, would that -- could you try to just say a few words, like "Dubra Noc" or "Dubra Dom" a bit louder so that the interpreters can hear you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I can try.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Is that good enough for the interpreters?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: No, Your Honour. Not really.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So we need, I'm afraid, the assistance of the technicians. Is it just the English booth that has problems? [French spoken]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Would you please count from 1 to 10 in order to test the system. I know for sure that you can.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7 --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Your Honour. There is interference, a lot of interference in our microphones.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Where does the interference come from? Could the technicians assist us? We still have to wait for a second since everything will be checked. Could you please repeat your counting from 1 to 10. I know that it's repetitious, but... Could you please do it again so that we can test the system.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: We can hear the witness, but there is still a lot of interference. On the other channel, there is no interference but we cannot hear the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: There still seems to be a lot of technical problems. I apologise for these technical difficulties. Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Perhaps I could avail myself of this opportunity just to speak for the French booth. And what they wanted is Mr. Ierace to come closer to the microphone when he speaks so that we don't have other problems.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, that's the problem we have with Mr. Ierace, but our main problem at this moment is -- is it of any use to retest the system?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'm informed that at this very moment, the technicians cannot achieve a better result as it is now. May I invite the English booth to do their utmost best and to let me know immediately if we cannot proceed any more. And I apologise already for the unpleasant circumstances you have to work under.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: We shall do what we can.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Please let me know if it really is impossible to continue. The English booth will do their utmost best to translate as good as they can. Mr. Ierace, would you please proceed, and perhaps if we would all keep in mind that it's not an easy task at this moment for the interpreters.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I do not know how much -- perhaps the French transcript can be placed on the computer, on the monitors in the English booth which could perhaps help them to work from the French transcript.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I've no idea whether this would be of any help, but if the booth would follow the suggestion, being supported by the transcript. But I'm afraid it's just the other way around, that you're not the source of the transcript, of course you can't do with. Let's try to proceed and see where we cannot continue any more. Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you continue to live in Sarajevo throughout the conflict?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In what part of Sarajevo were you living in 1993?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Would you please turn off your microphone whenever you are waiting for the answer, Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E
utterances.text: In the [redacted].

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Did you also live there, that is, in the old part of the town -- withdraw that. You've mentioned a street. In which area of Sarajevo did you live? Was that also Sedrenik?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Did you also live there in 1992 and 1994 and 1995?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I ask the witness be given a sheet of paper.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Usher. Yes, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was there an incident when you were at home and when you were shot?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E
utterances.text: Yes, there was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you please write on the piece of paper in front of you the date that you were shot.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, the colour of the marker is not of major importance at this moment.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Might I please have access to that piece of paper. Mr. President, I seek to tender that as a confidential exhibit. I think it would be P3654E, capital E, that is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And would you please show it to the Defence. Yes. I think since we deal with these kind of documents in the early stages, we'll admit it into evidence right away confidentially. That's P3654E. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, perhaps the reference to the street name might be redacted as well. That's page 47, line 16.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I'll ask Madam Registrar to prepare the decision to redact that part of the statement.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, at that time, having regard to your birth date, you were a child. Is that correct? But I do not want to know your exact age.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was the weather like on that day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E
utterances.text: It was sunny.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What were you wearing?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E
utterances.text: Dark trousers and a blue jacket.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At some stage in the morning, did you go outside to play?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Whereabouts did you play? Was it in the front yard, the back yard, or somewhere else?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E
utterances.text: Beneath the window of the house.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was that in the front yard?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After a while, were you joined by another child who played with you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I do not want to know his name. Was he of a similar age to you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: For how long did you play with him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E
utterances.text: Half an hour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he then leave?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The witness nods.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right. Just for the benefit of the transcript and what occurred, I think the witness also answer "yes," so there may be some further problems in hearing the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you please, Miss E, talk as loud as possible since the interpreters have some difficulties in hearing you. Again, I think the answer to the last question, when Mr. Ierace asked you, "Did he then leave?" Was "Yes." Is that true?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I did, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please proceed, Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How long after the boy left -- withdraw that. Were you and he both playing in the front yard for all of the period that he was with you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E
utterances.text: I didn't understand the question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You've told us that you were joined by another child, and that you and he played for about half an hour. Did you both play in the front yard for all of that half hour?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After he left, what did you do?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS E
